claim.value: Eligible accounts should be randomly assigned to the proposed change or the current flow if random assignment is feasible.
claim.scope: A feasibility-conditioned design proposal, not a report of actual randomization.

provenance.rationale: The span explicitly supplies the feasibility condition and both assignment alternatives.

signal_basis.value: Compare first-publication outcomes after release within a predefined observation window. Valid random assignment, comparable follow-up and reliable outcome capture allow a publication difference to support an effect of the change.
signal_basis.scope: Proposed observations among eligible accounts over their intended roster opportunity; interpretation requires comparable linkage and capture and adequate evidence.

provenance.rationale: The cited bundle supplies the proposed outcome comparison, observation window, causal interpretation conditions and evidence limitations.
The supported design proposal does not require an unresolved empirical relation to establish its warrant.

rationale: Random assignment is warranted as a feasible design for learning whether the change affects publication: it limits systematic assignment differences between the compared groups. The mapping explicitly connects this design to the outcome comparison and bounds causal interpretation. The claim neither reports completed randomization nor promises an improvement.
uncertainty: Feasibility is explicitly conditional. The size and direction of any release effect remain unknown without undermining the design proposal.
